school.tagged_body:
Your Dream Can Change

When I was eight, I wanted to be a {{v:firefighter}}. At eleven, I wanted to be a {{v:famous}} singer. Now I am fifteen, and I want to be a science teacher. Every time my dream changed, I felt a little {{v:embarrassed}}. {{g:I felt like I failed|feel like + 주어 + 동사: ~인 것처럼 느끼다}} at something.

But recently, I learned something. {{t:Dreams can change, and that is natural.}} {{g:As we grow older|as + 주어 + 동사: ~함에 따라}}, we learn more about the world and about ourselves. We find new {{v:interests}}. We also find out {{g:what we are really good at|관계대명사 what: ~하는 것 (= the thing that)}}. {{g:If our dreams never changed, that would be strange|가정법 과거: If + 과거동사, would + 동사원형 (현재 사실과 반대)}}.

My old dreams were not {{v:a waste of time}}. {{g:My dream of being a firefighter|전치사 of + 동명사(being): ~이 되는 것}} taught me that helping others is important. I practiced singing a lot, so now I can speak in front of people with {{v:confidence}}. These two experiences will {{g:help me become|help + 목적어 + 동사원형: ~가 …하도록 돕다}} a better teacher someday.

So don't worry if you don't have a clear dream yet. Don't worry if your dream {{g:keeps changing|keep + -ing: 계속 ~하다}}. You don't need the "right" answer now. Just keep {{v:exploring}}, try new things, and learn about yourself. {{t:Every step is part of your journey.}}

academy.tagged_body:
Your Dream Can Change

When I was eight, I wanted to be a firefighter. At eleven, I {{g:dreamed of becoming|dream of + 동명사: ~하는 것을 꿈꾸다}} a famous singer. Now, at fifteen, I want to be a science teacher. {{v:Whenever}} my dream changed, I felt a little {{v:embarrassed}}, {{g:as if I had failed|as if + 가정법 과거완료: 마치 ~했던 것처럼 (실제로는 실패하지 않음)}} at something.

Recently, however, I realized that {{g:changing dreams is completely natural|동명사 주어(changing dreams)는 단수 취급 → is}}. {{g:As we grow older|as + 주어 + 동사: ~함에 따라}}, we learn more about the world and about ourselves. We {{v:discover}} new interests and find out {{g:what we are truly good at|관계대명사 what: ~하는 것}}. {{g:It would actually be strange if our dreams stayed the same forever|가정법 과거: 주절 would + 동사원형, if절 과거동사}}.

Interestingly, {{t:none of my old dreams were a waste of time}}. Wanting to be a firefighter taught me {{g:how important it is to help others|간접의문문(how + 형용사 + 주어 + 동사) + 가주어 it / 진주어 to부정사}}. Practicing singing gave me the {{v:confidence}} to speak in front of people. Both of these experiences will {{g:help me become|help + 목적어 + 동사원형}} a better teacher someday.

So if you don't have a clear dream yet, or if your dream {{g:keeps changing|keep + -ing: 계속 ~하다}}, don't worry. {{g:What matters is not having the "right" answer now|관계대명사 what 주어(단수 취급) + 동명사 보어}}. What matters is continuing to {{v:explore}}, try new things, and learn about yourself. {{t:Every step you take is part of your journey.}}

advanced.tagged_body:
Your Dream Can Change

When I was eight years old, I wanted to become a firefighter. By the age of eleven, {{g:I had started dreaming of becoming|과거완료(had p.p.): 과거 시점(11살)까지 이미 일어난 일}} a famous singer. {{g:Now that I am fifteen|now that + 주어 + 동사: 이제 ~이므로}}, my goal is to become a science teacher. Each time my dream changed, I felt slightly {{v:embarrassed}}, {{g:as if I had failed|as if + 가정법 과거완료: 마치 ~했던 것처럼}} at something important.

Recently, however, {{g:I have come to realize|come to + 동사원형: ~하게 되다 / 현재완료}} that {{t:changing dreams is completely natural}}. As we grow older, we learn more about the world and discover more about ourselves. We develop new interests and find out what we are {{v:genuinely}} good at. In fact, {{g:it would be rather strange if our dreams remained exactly the same forever|가정법 과거: 현재 사실과 반대되는 가정}}.

Interestingly, none of my earlier dreams {{v:turned out to be}} a waste of time. {{g:My desire to become|to부정사의 형용사적 용법: ~하려는 열망}} a firefighter taught me {{g:how important it is to help others|간접의문문 + 가주어 it / 진주어 to부정사}}. Practicing singing gave me the confidence to speak in front of an {{v:audience}}. Both of these experiences will {{v:undoubtedly}} help me become a better teacher someday.

So if you do not have a clear dream yet, or if your dream keeps changing, there is no need to worry. {{g:What really matters is not finding the "right" answer immediately|관계대명사 what 주어 + 동명사 보어}}. prestudy.tagged_body:
Your Dream Can Change

At the age of eight, I {{v:aspired to become}} a firefighter. By eleven, I was fantasizing about becoming a {{v:renowned}} singer. Now, at fifteen, {{g:I am determined to become|be determined to + 동사원형: ~하기로 굳게 결심하다}} a science teacher. Whenever my {{v:aspirations}} shifted, I felt somewhat embarrassed, {{g:as though I had failed|as though + 가정법 과거완료: 마치 ~했던 것처럼}} at something significant.

Recently, however, {{t:I have come to recognize that changing one's dreams is an entirely natural process}}. As we mature, we {{v:accumulate}} knowledge about the world and gain a deeper understanding of ourselves. We encounter unfamiliar interests and identify {{g:what we are genuinely capable of|관계대명사 what + 전치사 of로 끝나는 절}}. Indeed, {{g:it would be peculiar if our dreams remained unchanged|가정법 과거 + 가주어 it}} throughout our entire lives.

Remarkably, none of my previous dreams {{v:proved to be}} a waste of time. {{g:Aspiring to be a firefighter|동명사 주어(단수 취급) → taught}} taught me {{g:how essential it is to assist others|간접의문문 + 가주어 it / 진주어 to부정사}}. Practicing singing, meanwhile, {{g:provided me with|provide A with B: A에게 B를 제공하다}} the confidence to speak in front of an audience. Both of these experiences will undoubtedly {{g:contribute to making|contribute to + 동명사 (to는 전치사)}} me a better teacher someday.

Therefore, if {{g:you have yet to discover|have yet to + 동사원형: 아직 ~하지 않았다}} a clear dream, or if your dream continues to {{v:evolve}}, there is no reason for concern. {{g:What truly matters is not possessing the "correct" answer|관계대명사 what 주어 + not A, rather B 구조}} at this particular moment. Rather, what matters is continuing to explore, experimenting with unfamiliar things, and deepening your understanding of yourself. {{t:Every step you take constitutes a valuable part of your journey.}}

However, the writer realized that changing dreams is natural and that each old dream taught something valuable. The writer advises readers not to worry and to keep exploring themselves.

essays.q: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오. '중요한 것은 정답을 갖는 것이 아니라 계속 탐색하는 것이다.' <조건> 관계대명사 what으로 시작하고 not A but B를 사용할 것
essays.sampleAnswer: What matters is not having the right answer but continuing to explore.

essays.q: Some people say teenagers should decide on their future careers as early as possible. Do you agree? Write your opinion in English, referring to the passage.
essays.sampleAnswer: I disagree. As the passage says, we gain a deeper understanding of ourselves as we mature, so an early decision may not reflect who we really are. Moreover, even dreams we give up can teach us valuable skills. Therefore, teenagers should explore various interests before making a final decision.
essays.rubric: ① 찬반 입장 명확 ② 본문 내용을 근거로 활용 ③ 논리적 연결어 사용 ④ 영어 문장의 정확성

wordbook.sentence: At the age of eight, I aspired to become a firefighter.
By eleven, I was fantasizing about becoming a renowned singer.
Whenever my aspirations shifted, I felt somewhat embarrassed, as though I had failed at something significant.
As we mature, we accumulate knowledge about the world and gain a deeper understanding of ourselves.
Remarkably, none of my previous dreams proved to be a waste of time.
Therefore, if you have yet to discover a clear dream, or if your dream continues to evolve, there is no reason for concern.
